newsitem.title: UK: Shell lines up for chance of more Nigeria oil assets.
newsitem.headline: Shell lines up for chance of more Nigeria oil assets.

text.p: Royal/Dutch Shell Group would seriously consider buying more Nigerian upstream oil assets if the government proceeds with the sale of its majority share in joint-venture production companies, group managing director Cor Herkstroter said on Thursday.
"(We would) seriously look at it, no doubt," Herkstroter told reporters at a briefing on Thursday.

A phased five-year sale of Nigerian National Petroleum Corp's (NNPC) average 57 percent share in six joint ventures with Shell and five other international oil companies was proposed by finance minister Anthony Ani in September last year.
Oil companies are anxiously awaiting Nigeria's budget statement, due any time now, for clues on whether the privatisation will proceed.
Shell has easily the biggest operation in Nigeria, pumping about a million barrels a day in partnership with NNPC.
The company came under heavy criticism for its Nigerian operations after Nigeria's military governmnet hanged author Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other Ogoni minority rights activists in November 1995.
